subject: SentinelAI launch quota & surge coordination
messages:
From: Marcus Lin <marcus@redwood.com>
To: karthik_iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, soojin_lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com>, kimberly_park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>, monica_patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 08 Dec 2026 14:02:00 -0800
Subject: SentinelAI launch: quota ask and surge profile — need product/infra confirmation

Team,

Heads-up: SentinelAI (contact: Elena Torres) is targeting a staged launch the week of 12/14. They sent over an initial surge profile (attached) and an SLA amendment draft. High-level asks from their side: a temporary uplift in ingress quota for the first 72 hours and a predictable fallback plan if capacity becomes tight.

Summary of the customer-provided numbers (see attached Sentinel_Surge_Profile.xlsx):
- Staged ramp starting 12/14 00:00 UTC.
- Expected steady-state: ~1,200 concurrent users.
- Peak ingress: ~350 requests/sec for a 30-min spike window on day 1.
- Median request size: ~520 tokens in, ~110 tokens out (high variance).

What we need from infra/product (please):
1) Confirm if we can accommodate a temporary rate window of 400 RPS for 72 hours starting 12/14. If not, what alternative uplift can we guarantee?
2) Recommend a fallback model variant we can route to automatically (quantized or smaller checkpoint) and the expected unit-cost delta.
3) Any limitations with KV/prefix caching for this workload — the customer expects some repeated prompts but not perfectly identical.
4) Ops runbook items we should include in the DocuSign SLA (attached SLA-Amendment_v2.pdf).

Attachments: Sentinel_Surge_Profile.xlsx, SLA-Amendment_v2.pdf

Proposed next step: quick sync tomorrow (12/09) to lock in uplift and routing policy. If product/infra can respond in-thread with rough capacity suggestions and any blockers, that would be great.

Thanks,
Marcus Lin
Sr. Sales Engineer, Redwood Inference
marcus@redwood.com

--

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus@redwood.com>, soojin_lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com>, kimberly_park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>, monica_patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 09 Dec 2026 09:15:00 -0800
Subject: Re: SentinelAI launch: quota ask and surge profile — need product/infra confirmation

On Tue, Dec 8, 2026 at 2:02 PM Marcus Lin <marcus@redwood.com> wrote:
> Team,
> 
> Heads-up: SentinelAI (contact: Elena Torres) is targeting a staged launch the week of 12/14...

Thanks Marcus — good summary. Quick infra read:
- Current hosted pools have headroom for small bursts but not sustained 400 RPS on top of normal traffic without reserved capacity.
- For a safe 72-hour uplift we should provision a small Dedicated pool (suggestion: 4 x A100-equivalent cards) that can be isolated for the ramp window. That gives us predictable throughput and avoids impacting other customers.
- Autoscaling warm-up for dedicated instances is non-zero; expect ~5–7 minutes to reach steady-state after spin-up requests.

To size this properly we need:
- Expected peak concurrent inference contexts (not just users). If 1,200 users map to ~1,200 active contexts, peak token throughput at 350 RPS * (520+110) tokens/request ~= 219,500 tokens/sec — that seems high; please confirm token counts and whether the 520 includes system tokens.
- Expected distribution (what percent of requests are short vs long).

Operational fallback: we can configure automatic routing to a quantized fp16->int8 variant (model: sentinel-base-q8_0) if we detect 95th percentile latency crossing our p95 SLO or if queue length exceeds threshold. That will reduce GPU utilization by ~30% at cost of slightly noisier outputs — product needs to sign off for customer.

Cost note: Dedicated reserved for 72 hours + data egress will be a non-trivial delta; attach a quick cost csv if you want (I can run numbers).

Will wait on the token clarification and sample traffic CSV (per-request distribution) before we commit. We should also confirm whether the customer accepts graceful degradation (fallback model + headroom) or requires hard rate limits.

-karthik
Karthik Iyer
Principal Infra PM, Redwood Inference

From: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus@redwood.com>, karthik_iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, kimberly_park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>, monica_patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 09 Dec 2026 11:40:00 -0800
Subject: Re: SentinelAI launch: quota ask and surge profile — need product/infra confirmation

Thanks for looping us in. A few product points / clarifying questions:

1) Fallback model and quality gates
- If infra routes to sentinel-base-q8_0 we need a clear definition of the quality gate. Recommend: canary 10% of traffic for first 6 hours, then increase to 50% if error/loss metrics stable.
- Product needs to know which metrics the customer will accept as success: p95 latency < 350ms, generation error rate (incomplete outputs) < 0.5%, semantic regression tolerance of < 5% on our diff metric.

2) Caching behavior
- KV/prefix caching benefits require high prompt repeatability. If their prompts have personalization tokens/IDs, effective cache hit rate may be < 10%. Please ask them to share a 48–72 hour sample of representative requests (anonymized) so we can estimate hit rates.

3) Routing & rollout policy
- We can provide a temporary route policy: primary -> high-throughput pool; fallback -> quantized variant with automatic reversion when latency recovers for 15 consecutive minutes. This will require a short feature flag toggle and a canary window.
- Model switchover testing: we need at least a 24-hour internal dry run on staging to validate fidelity of quantized variant for their prompts. Can we schedule that this week?

4) Telemetry and alerting
- Recommend these watch windows: token/sec, GPU utilization, queue depth, p50/p95/p99 latency, 5xx error rate. Set alert thresholds with paging at sustained p95 > 500ms for 5 minutes.

I can draft the minimal product acceptance criteria to insert into the SLA if you want — will add to runbook once we have the sample traffic.

Soojin Lee
Product Manager, Model Serving

From: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>

> 
> Elena Torres

Two asks from me:
- Can infra confirm whether a 4x-A100 dedicated carveout is enough for the 400 RPS target? If not, suggest final number & explain delivery constraints.

Subject: RE: SentinelAI launch: quota ask and surge profile — need product/infra confirmation

All — update and final operational commitments for the launch window.

After sizing conversation with infra and product:
- Temporary uplift approved: 400 RPS window for 72 hours starting 2026-12-14 00:00 UTC (ends 2026-12-17 00:00 UTC).
- Implementation: provision Dedicated pool (4 x A100-equivalent) + pre-warm 30 minutes before start time. Autoscale fallback is configured to spin additional capacity if queue length > 1200 for > 3 minutes, but we will rely on the dedicated carveout as primary.
- Fallback policy: automatic reroute to sentinel-base-q8_0 when p95 latency > 450ms for 5 consecutive minutes or 5xx error rate > 0.5%; product will run the 24-hour dry run on staging by 12/12.

Runbook / artifacts attached: launch-runbook.md (playbook), Launch-Cost-Delta.csv (pricing estimate), SLA-Amendment_v2.pdf. HubSpot/deal: https://app.hubspot.com/deals/4821. DocuSign (customer signature in progress): https://www.docusign.com/embedded-signer/abc123

Operational notes / next steps:
- Marcus / Kimberly: confirm start time window with SentinelAI's PM and ensure they send the anonymized 48–72 hour sample traffic by EOD 12/11 so product can finalize cache estimates.
- Karthik: please file a short postmortem template and enable the alerting thresholds Soojin suggested.
- Product: after the 24-hour staging run (target 12/12), sign off in-thread so we can flip feature flags and pre-provision.

I'll schedule a 30-minute kickoff for 12/13 to run through roles and paging.

Thanks — we should be set if the customer signs today.

Monica Patel
Customer Operations Manager, Redwood Inference
